ai.description: Blanford's Rock Agama reaches 10 cm snout-vent length. Males display bright red heads and throats during breeding; females are mottled brown. Both sexes feature a distinct nuchal crest and granular scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: Distinguish *Psammophilus blanfordanus* by the distinct, enlarged, and sharply keeled scales on its nape and back, which form a prominent, spiny crest absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: Blanford's Rock Agama inhabits rocky outcrops and boulder-strewn hillsides in dry deciduous forests and scrublands, typically at elevations between 300 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: Blanford's Rock Agamas are diurnal lizards that frequently perform conspicuous "push-up" displays on rocky outcrops to signal dominance and defend their territories.
ai.reproductionNotes: Blanford's Rock Agama is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 3–8 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally between June and September.
ai.distributionRemarks: Blanford's Rock Agama is endemic to peninsular India, primarily inhabiting rocky outcrops in the Eastern Ghats and Deccan Plateau at elevations up to 1,500 meters.
